title: The 1924 letter from Joe Oliver
summary: Oliver writes inviting Lee to Chicago after Lorenzo Tio's recommendation; Lee accepts at once.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: They was kids then, just learning how to play trombone at that time. 1924, I got a letter from Joe Oliver. Joe Oliver was telling me that Lewis had quit him and was, was, had gone to work to Dreamlin, but was talking about leaving and going to New York City. And he'd say, uh, Lorenzo Teo had wrote and told Joe Oliver about the progress that I was making on my cornered, cause Joe had asked, who's all the battle house cornered players down there that could play like bunk and uh, all the good old boys. Lorenzo told him, say, Lee Collins is about the best they got in jazz down here now. So Joe wrote me a letter and asked me, how about, how would I like to come to Chicago to work at the Lincoln Garden? He would hear me say, he said, I couldn't, I couldn't hardly finish, I didn't even finish reading the letter. I said, could I come to Chicago to work with him? I stopped reading the letter. So I went right on the way. That, at that time, I talked it over to my first wife at that time and asked her, I say, I got a chance to go to Chicago with Joe Oliver, what, how about me, what you think about me going to jail? And she got knocked out about it. She said, Jesus, we both, we walked around in a daze for about an hour before we could say anything. So I go, I make some beeline right from the Western Union. And I go to the Western Union, I send Joe a telegram and tell him I sound like very much to come to Chicago, join him at the Lincoln Garden. So Joe Oliver looked like before I could get back home I had a ticket there. Joe got the telegram and he said, send me a ticket, told me to come at once. So I go to Chicago, first time, and to play with Joe. So I go to Chicago with Baby Dodds and Johnny Dodds and all of them had to quit Joe at that time. They were Baby Dodds and they was working down at Kelly's table, and Johnny Dodds, let me tell you about that.
Yeah, and where was your job?
